path: App Store Reviews/33. Habitify - Habit Tracker - Daily Goals, Routine & Streaks/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Great Habit Tracker!
record.body:
My yearly Strides subscription came up and took a look at my options. This app is on point. I’m switching. 

One of my gripes with other apps is you could not set your day to be anything other than resetting at 12am. Shame because maybe your ‘day’ finishes a bit later. This app does that. No more manual entry! : )

Another thing I didn’t like with the competition was that there was no organization set for each period of day. I have a morning routine, things I do during the day and evening. This app does that if you want AND you can adjust the time for each period of the day. Genius! With other apps I had to organize it myself with tags and the experience was not great nor fluid, or simply was not available and I’d just have a list. 

Plus there is a web and Mac app and the price is reasonable by comparison as well. Nice settings for habit tracking and notifications too. Great job! Thank you for a great app. I’m getting Life-Time Premium  ❤️😇✌️

record.title: 改善して欲しい点が２つ
record.body:
概ね満足して使っていますが、改善して欲しい点が２つあります！
1つ目は、カテゴリーの並び替えをできるようにしてほしいということ。カテゴリーの並び替えができないと、例えば、「朝活」のカテゴリーの下に「寝る前の習慣」が表示されてしまうなど、不自然になってしまうことがあります。
2つ目は、午前、午後、夜だけでなく、時間帯を自分で細かく分けられるようにしてほしいということ。
人によって、時間帯の区分は様々だと思うので、自分てわ自由に設定できれば、例えば、「通勤時間」とか「昼休み」のような時間帯の設定もできるようになってさらに便利になると思います。
買い切り版を購入していて、今後も長く使っていきたいと思っているアプリなので、是非改善お願いします。

record.title: The update made the UI clunkier
record.body:
I’m not sure why this app was recently updated to add extra taps in order to navigate. I used to be able to instantly tap on any other day of the week in the top bar, and to also swipe left or right to choose days even further ahead or behind. I used to be able to swipe left or right on habit’s month views and see other months.

Now I have to tap a disclosure triangle to show the top bar first. And in month view, to get to another month, I have to open a menu, and choose from a list of just six months. If I want to look at a month prior to April 2020 to see my habits, guess what... I can’t. The app has been updated not only to make things take more time, but to make it literally impossible to see data I used to be able to see in a matter of seconds.

Why did you guys make this change??

path: App Store Reviews/31. Do Habits - Get It Done - Daily Routine & Goal Planner/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Beautifully and simply design, solid goal tracker
record.body:
I love this app! I’ve been using this for a few months to help track goals. It’s simple to use, while still having a solid set of features. It allows you to tack both goals you’re building towards (ex. Daily meditation, exercising 4x/week) or trying to quit/reduce (ex. Quit drinking). I paid for the upgrade so I could track more goals after I hit the limit because I was finding it actually helped me keep motivated. (And also to get upgrades on two of their other awesome apps - Grateful and Moody)

My three feature requests (stack ranked)  

1. Goals are sorted alphabetically and you can’t rearrange them. What I want is a way to view all my goals grouped by category. For example, I want to see my physical health goals (exercise 4x/week, eat healthy) grouped and my personal enrichment goals (meditate daily, read daily, journal 2x/week) grouped. It does allow you to tag goals with categories and filter by category, but I don’t find the filtering useful because I want to see all the goals at once. This would give me a birds eye view of how I’m doing in different parts of my life (physical health, mental health, hobbies, etc.). 

2. Integrations with your other apps, Moody and Grateful. For example I want to see a goal to enter my mood three times a day and make an entry in Moody daily. I would like Done to automatically know when I’ve completed those goals in the other apps.

Currently the app has bar charts for your goals. For the types of goals I’m tracking, I don’t find this visualization particularly helpful. For example, if I hurt my daily meditation goal every day for a month it’s just a bunch of equal height bars. I do like the idea of visualizing data on my goals and hope you do more explorations there. 

Overall an awesome app! (If anyone who works there reads this, I signed up for Beta and would be happy to participate in research!)

record.title: Like having a personal assistant (or a nagging significant other) with me at all times!
record.body:
The app is very well thought out. Animation and iconography are superb and make the app very organic and fun to use. The intelligent use of animation gives the app a sense of speed and effortlessness that is sure to please chronic procrastinators such as myself. 

The one thing I think could be added is an option for bedtime reminders. 

I use the "evening" category for things I want to do after the work day, but not necessarily before bed. 

I would like to be able to create a "before bed" routine (read, brush teeth, drink some water, stretch) that I don't want to clutter the evening category with. 

Other than this, I was pleasantly surprised with this app and bought the full version within 5 minutes of playing around with the app since it felt so solid. 

Thank you for helping me be a greater person, one habit at a time!

record.title: Simple to use
record.body:
This is simple to use which means I am more likely to use it.

I would like a snooze option when it reminds me since most often I am in the middle of something and cannot do my habit right away.  Maybe I should leave the notification open but I hate leaving open notifications on my screen.

Also, I have meds that I take 4 times a day but the app only gives me 3 timeslots.  I would prefer a "wakeup",  "lunch", "dinner", "bedtime" schedule for my meds but also keep the existing slots for other habits.

Finally, it would be more intuitive for me if I click on a habit with multiple times for it to take me to the screen where I can complete just one instance of that habit.  There is an icon at the bottom to do this but it would be more intuitive to click the main habit itself.
